subject: EU Data Subject Export & Deletion — action items for Acme user
messages:
From: Jane Doe <privacy@acme.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-18T09:15:00+00:00
Subject: Data subject request — export + deletion for user123@acme.com

Hi Kimberly,

We are submitting a data subject request (access + deletion) for one of our end users: user123@acme.com. Please confirm receipt and provide the export of all personal data Redwood holds for that identifier, and a certificate that deletion has been completed once processed.

A few context points: Acme is the data controller for our application; the request comes from our DPO (copied). Let us know typical turnaround and identity verification steps you require. We are under the EU DSR timeframe (one month).

Thanks,
Jane Doe
DPO — Acme Corp
privacy@acme.com

--
Attachment: identity-form-acme.pdf (stub)

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: Jane Doe <privacy@acme.com>
Cc: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-18T10:03:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Data subject request — export + deletion for user123@acme.com

Hi Jane — thanks for the request. Confirming receipt. High level plan below: 

- Verification: We need the controller-signed request and one piece of corroborating info for the subject (e.g., account creation timestamp or last 4 of phone). If you already attached identity-form-acme.pdf I can route it to privacy ops, but we typically ask controller-signed requests to avoid delays.
- Export: We'll produce a machine-readable export (JSONL) containing account attributes, message/content metadata, and delivery logs.
- Deletion: Once you confirm verification, we will queue a deletion job. Redwood issues a deletion certificate when data is removed from primary and cache layers; hard-delete from backups may follow our retention window as described in the DPA.

Target timelines: export within 5 business days after verification, deletion certificate within 10 business days. If you need acceleration, tell us and we can route as high priority.

Looping in Stephanie (legal) to confirm controller/processor note and Vivek (privacy ops) for the export package.

–Kimberly Park
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0119

Attachment: none

From: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: Jane Doe <privacy@acme.com>, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-18T12:22:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Data subject request — export + deletion for user123@acme.com

Thanks Kimberly — a few legal clarifications for the record that you can share with Acme: 

1) Roles: For typical usage of Redwood’s hosted API, Acme (the customer) is the controller for end-user content and Redwood is the processor. Where Redwood processes Customer Content to provide the service, we act under the terms of our DPA. This means we follow controller instructions for responding to DSRs submitted by the controller on behalf of a data subject.

2) SCCs / DPA: Requests should reference the DPA and SCCs in place (link below) for any cross-border processing questions. We will include the export package and a deletion certificate consistent with the DPA.

3) Evidence: For audit purposes Acme often asks for an export bundle + a short log excerpt showing deletion job execution and timestamps. We can provide a redacted log excerpt (IP and other non-essential telemetry redacted) as part of the package.

Action for Acme: please confirm the controller-signed request (email from corporate DPO address is fine) and confirm the exact subject identifier (we have user123@acme.com but please confirm user ID in your system, e.g., Acme internal id 98324).

Link to DPA (public): https://drive.redwood.com/share/dpa-acme-dpa-v2.pdf

–Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com

From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
To: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: Jane Doe <privacy@acme.com>
Date: 2026-12-19T08:45:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Data subject request — export + deletion for user123@acme.com

Operational note & deliverables: 

- Verification: once we receive the controller-signed confirmation we will mark the request as authorized in PRIV queue PRIV-4567.
- Export bundle: will include: account profile (profile fields, metadata), service request logs (request_id, timestamp, model_id, token counts), and user-generated content as stored. Sensitive runtime logs will be redacted. Filename: acme_user_export_user123_20261220.jsonl
- Deletion: we will perform deletion in three layers: primary DB, cache (KV cache), and a metadata tombstone. Backup removal follows retention schedule; deletion certificate will explicitly call out the layers removed and any backup retention caveats. Filename: deletion_certificate_user123_20261220.pdf
- Audit log excerpt: we can provide a single-day log excerpt showing the deletion job run and job-id (redacted): log_excerpt_user123_20261220.txt

Estimated ETA after verification: export delivered in 48–72 hours (depends on size); deletion certificate within 7 calendar days. If Acme requires a documented SLA exception we can escalate but that will involve a formal request through sales/legal.

Vivek Kulkarni
Privacy Ops Lead, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com

Attachment: none

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com

Date: 2026-12-20T13:05:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Data subject request — export + deletion for user123@acme.com

Hi Jane — thanks for the confirmation from Acme DPO (received earlier today). Per the verification we have produced the export bundle and queued the deletion job. Deliverables (attached):

- acme_user_export_user123_20261220.jsonl — machine-readable export containing attributes, non-sensitive logs, and stored content.
- deletion_certificate_user123_20261220.pdf — certificate describing layers deleted and retention caveats.
- log_excerpt_user123_20261220.txt — redacted excerpt showing deletion job id PRIV-4567-JB and timestamp 2026-12-20T12:48:09Z.

Summary of next steps: 
1) Please confirm receipt of the bundle.
2) If you require a further redaction pass or a different export format (CSV, XML), let us know.
3) If Acme needs explicit backup purge evidence beyond the retention note in the DPA, we can discuss escalation.

Ticket: PRIV-4567 (https://redwood-internal.atlassian.net/browse/PRIV-4567)

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme_user_export_user123_20261220.jsonl, deletion_certificate_user123_20261220.pdf, log_excerpt_user123_20261220.txt

Kimberly — received all three files, thank you. Quick follow-up: can you also provide a short confirmation that the deletion job removed associated KV cache entries (we rely on cached embeddings for personalization) — the log excerpt references cache invalidation but not the cache keys. If you can include either a short statement in the deletion certificate or a separate log line with the job id that enumerates which cache namespaces were targeted, that would be helpful for our internal audit.

Jane
DPO — Acme Corp
